title: Commodity Trend CTA — Bayesian Short+Long Signal Decomposition
source: arXiv:2507.15876 (2025) — 'Re-evaluating Short- and Long-Term Trend Factors in CTA Replication: A Bayesian Graphical Approach'
rationale: H261b CONFIRMED (OOS Sharpe 0.922, Corr(SPY)=0.218) but has a significant IS/OOS disconnect (IS Sharpe 0.256, commodity bear 2010-2017). The referenced paper shows CTAs blend short-term (~3m) and long-term (~12m) trend signals independently. Adding a 12m signal alongside H261b's 6m signal may improve IS performance by reducing whipsawing in gradual commodity bear markets — the 12m signal would shift to BIL earlier when a multi-year commodity bear sets in, while the 6m signal captures shorter-cycle opportunities. The Bayesian blend (vs 50/50) can be approximated by equal-weighting IS-optimized signal windows. This extends H261b without changing the universe.

design.universe: GLD, SLV, DBC, USO, DBA (same as H261b)
design.blend: Equal-weight rank scores from all 3 signals → composite rank → Top-2 positive absolute momentum gate (any 2 of 3 signals positive)
design.alternative: IS-optimize signal weights on 3m/6m/12m; freeze weights; apply OOS

confirm_gates.is_sharpe: > 0.50 (key: fix IS weakness — H261b IS was 0.256)

hypothesis_log_entry.note: Bayesian short+long CTA decomposition extending H261b. Blend 3m/6m/12m momentum signals for commodity Top-2 strategy. Aim: fix IS Sharpe=0.256 weakness while maintaining OOS Sharpe > 0.922 and Corr(SPY) < 0.50. Source: arXiv:2507.15876 CTA factor decomposition.
